scheme_name: Promotion of Patriotism/National Integration/Communal Harmony - Interschool Choreographic Dance Competition
description:
The Promotion of Patriotism/National Integration/Communal Harmony - Interschool Choreographic Dance Competition is an initiative launched by the Government of India to foster a sense of unity and cultural appreciation among school students across the country. 

This scheme was introduced in the year 2018 as part of the broader efforts to promote national integration and communal harmony among the youth. 

The competition aims to encourage students to express their patriotism and cultural diversity through choreographed dance performances. 

The objectives of this competition include enhancing students' understanding of the importance of national integration and communal harmony. 

The competition also seeks to instill a sense of pride in the rich cultural heritage of India among the youth. 

The measurable targets of the competition include participation from at least 1,000 schools across various states and union territories. 

The competition is designed to be held annually, with specific timelines for each edition announced by the implementing authorities. 

Benefits of participating in this competition include recognition at the national level for schools and students. 

Winners of the competition are awarded certificates and trophies, which serve as a form of encouragement for further participation in cultural activities. 

Additionally, the competition provides a platform for students to showcase their artistic talents and creativity. 

Eligibility criteria for participation in the competition include being a student of a recognized school in India. 

Students from classes 6 to 12 are eligible to participate, ensuring that a wide age range is included. 

There are no specific income criteria for students to participate in this competition. 

The application process for the competition involves schools registering their students through an online portal set up by the Ministry of Education. 

Schools must submit a detailed entry form that includes information about the participating students and the choreographed piece they intend to perform. 

The required documents for application include a school registration certificate and a list of participating students with their class and section details. 

The application deadline is typically set two months before the scheduled date of the competition. 

Once the applications are received, schools are notified about the selection process and the guidelines for the competition. 

The competition is conducted in multiple stages, including preliminary rounds at the district level followed by state-level competitions. 

The final competition is held at a national venue, where selected teams from each state compete for the top honors. 

The frequency of the competition is annual, with specific dates announced each year. 

For example, the 2023 edition of the competition was scheduled to take place in October, with preliminary rounds starting in August. 

The implementing authority for this competition is the Ministry of Education, Government of India. 

The National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) also plays a significant role in organizing and promoting the event. 

Schools interested in participating can contact the Ministry of Education through their official website for further information. 

The competition not only promotes patriotism but also encourages students to learn about various cultural dance forms from different regions of India. 

This exposure helps students appreciate the diversity of Indian culture and fosters communal harmony. 

The competition also aims to develop teamwork and collaboration skills among students as they work together to create their performances. 

In 2022, over 1,200 schools participated in the competition, showcasing a variety of dance forms including classical, folk, and contemporary styles. 

The initiative has received positive feedback from educators and parents alike, highlighting its role in promoting cultural education. 

In addition to the competition, workshops and training sessions are often organized to help students improve their dance skills and learn about choreography. 

These workshops are conducted by experienced choreographers and educators who provide guidance on various dance techniques. 

The competition also serves as a platform for schools to network and collaborate on cultural initiatives beyond the competition itself. 

Participating schools often report an increase in student engagement in cultural activities as a result of their involvement in the competition. 

The competition also aligns with the National Education Policy 2020, which emphasizes the importance of arts and culture in education. 

By integrating cultural education into the school curriculum, the government aims to create a more holistic learning environment for students. 

The competition has also seen participation from schools in remote and rural areas, ensuring inclusivity in cultural representation. 

The government encourages schools to incorporate local cultural elements into their performances, further promoting regional diversity. 

Feedback from participants indicates that the competition has significantly boosted their confidence and public speaking skills. 

The competition is also covered by various media outlets, providing students with recognition and visibility for their talents. 

In conclusion, the Promotion of Patriotism/National Integration/Communal Harmony - Interschool Choreographic Dance Competition is a vital initiative aimed at fostering unity and cultural appreciation among Indian youth. 

Through this competition, the government seeks to instill a sense of pride in India's diverse cultural heritage while promoting national integration. 

With its structured application process and clear eligibility criteria, the competition provides an accessible platform for students to engage in artistic expression. 

The initiative not only benefits participants but also enriches the cultural fabric of the nation by celebrating its diversity and promoting communal harmony. 

As the competition continues to grow in participation and recognition, it plays a crucial role in shaping the cultural landscape of India's educational institutions. 

The ongoing support from the Ministry of Education and other implementing agencies ensures the sustainability and success of this important initiative. 

Overall, the competition serves as a beacon of hope for fostering a united and harmonious society through the arts.
